issues.legal_issue: A successor sovereign is not bound by a liability incurred by a former sovereign before territorial merger unless the successor expressly or impliedly accepts the claim, even when the liability concerns public property retained by the successor.
material_facts: Builders constructed public court and secretariat buildings for the former state, and its ruler admitted the amount claimed and executed a promissory note for it.
After the former state merged into the successor state, the successor took possession of and retained the buildings as public property.
The successor state had not expressly or impliedly undertaken to pay the claim.
issues.conclusion: The claim could not be enforced against the successor state because it had not accepted the liability; the Act of State defence was available, including in respect of liability concerning public property retained by the successor.
issues.legal_principle: An Act of State is an exercise of sovereign power over territory not previously subject to that sovereign. Following acquisition or merger, inhabitants may enforce only rights the new sovereign has recognized, and the defence ends only upon express or implied acceptance of the claim. The principle applies even to liabilities concerning public property of the former state that the successor takes over and retains. The Court relied on Raja Rajender Chand v. Sukhi, State of Saurashtra v. Memon Haji Ismail, and Vaje Singh Ji Joravar Singh v. Secretary of State for India in Council.

rule.if: successor_state_claim and territory_newly_acquired and former_state_liability and public_property_retained and not successor_acceptance

predicates.successor_state_claim: A claimant seeks to enforce against a successor sovereign a liability associated with a former sovereign.
predicates.territory_newly_acquired: The territory in which the liability arose came under the successor sovereign's authority for the first time.
predicates.former_state_liability: The liability was incurred by or on behalf of the former sovereign before the territorial change.
predicates.public_property_retained: The successor sovereign took over and retained as public property property connected with the liability.
predicates.successor_acceptance: The successor sovereign expressly or impliedly accepted the claim or undertook to honour the liability.
predicates.successor_state_not_bound: The successor sovereign is not bound to pay the unaccepted former-state liability.

issues.definition: When a claim against a successor sovereign concerns a former sovereign's liability incurred in newly acquired territory, retention of connected public property does not bind the successor if it has not accepted the claim.

issues.legal_issue: A successor state's request for details to examine a claim does not, without acceptance of the claim, amount to acceptance of the liability or waiver of the Act of State defence.
material_facts: The successor state asked the claimants to provide details of their claim and was prepared to consider it.
The successor state did not accept the claim or undertake to pay the liability.
issues.conclusion: The request for details and willingness to consider the claim did not amount to acceptance of the liability or waiver of the Act of State defence.
issues.legal_principle: A new sovereign may investigate a claim and decide whether to honour it without thereby accepting it or abandoning the Act of State defence. Acceptance, express or implied, is what brings that defence to an end. The Court relied on the principles discussed in Raja Rajender Chand v. Sukhi, State of Saurashtra v. Memon Haji Ismail, and Vaje Singh Ji Joravar Singh v. Secretary of State for India in Council.

rule.if: successor_state_claim and claim_details_requested and claim_considered and not claim_accepted

predicates.successor_state_claim: A claimant seeks to enforce against a successor sovereign a liability associated with a former sovereign.
predicates.claim_details_requested: The successor sovereign asked the claimant to provide details supporting the claim.
predicates.claim_considered: The successor sovereign was prepared to examine whether to honour the claim.
predicates.claim_accepted: The successor sovereign expressly or impliedly accepted the claim or undertook to pay the liability.
predicates.inquiry_does_not_waive_act_of_state_defe: The successor sovereign's inquiry into the claim does not waive its Act of State defence.

issues.definition: When a successor sovereign requests details and considers a claim without accepting it, that inquiry does not waive its Act of State defence.
